title: ZPA policy evaluation
aliases: why was access blocked in zpa

prose.text: "Why was this ZPA request allowed or blocked?" needs five questions answered in order.

steps.label: Which policy types run, and in what order?
steps.text: Client forwarding comes before access, a bypass skips access, and each type has a default when nothing matches: [[zpa.policy.evaluation-order]].

steps.label: Which application segment did the request map to?
steps.text: The most specific one, unless Multimatch is on: [[zpa.policy.multimatch]].

steps.label: Which rule is first?
steps.text: First match by rule order, with the Deception exception: [[zpa.policy.access-rule-order]].

steps.label: Do the rule's criteria match?
steps.text: The criteria, their combinations and limits: [[zpa.policy.criteria]]; the AND and OR logic and operand forms: [[zpa.policy.conditions]].

prose.text: Segment matching is also covered in [[zpa.app-segments.matching]]. Segment groups in rules are covered in [[zpa.segment-groups.policy-use]], and microtenant evaluation in [[zpa.microtenants.policy-evaluation]]. Identity criteria are covered in [[zpa.saml-attributes.policy-criteria]] and [[zpa.scim.policy-criteria]], with SCIM sync timing in [[zpa.scim.provisioning-timing]]. Trusted networks, machine groups and federated rules are covered in [[zpa.trusted-networks.policy-operand]], [[zpa.machine-groups.policy-use]] and [[zpa.b2b-federation.access-policy]].

Session timing is a separate rule set: [[zpa.policy.timeout-rules]]. Rule fields beyond criteria are in [[zpa.policy.rule-fields]]. SCIM criteria depend on sync timing: [[zpa.policy.scim-sync]]. Common rule layouts are in [[zpa.policy.patterns]].
How Terraform orders and writes these rules is in [[zpa.terraform.rule-order]] and [[zpa.terraform.policy-rule-writes]]. The server group a rule may name is in [[zpa.server-groups]].
